newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS prices fall in light pre-holiday talk.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS prices fall in light pre-holiday talk.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices fell modestly in light ACCESS trade Thursday, as overnight traders were absent from the market ahead of next week's Christmas holiday, dealers said.
"The lack of participation might help correct crude prices a little bit," a trader said, noting the recent run-up in NYMEX crude left the front-month futures contract overbought.
He said "Holiday trading" had set in, a term which meant the market turned inactive as traders squared books before the holidays.
January crude oil traded at $25.31 a barrel, down 14 cents a barrel from the settle amid trade of 313 contracts. About 401 contracts traded overall.
January heating oil shed 0.28 cent a gallon to 73.50 cents amid light volume of 142 contracts in January and 199 contracts overall.
Front-month gasoline eased 0.22 cent to 71 cents a gallon, as 120 lots traded in the nearby month and 272 were exchanged overall.
